subject: SIG3: runtime telemetry extract & KMS custody -- subprocessor list request

From: Helen Park <helen.park@novamed.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: NovaMed Security <security@novamed.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SIG3 runtime telemetry extract & KMS custody / subprocessor roster

Rachel / Redwood team,

As part of NovaMed's SIG3 intake for our procurement approval, we need two items to complete the security review: a current roster of all runtime subprocessors that touch or can access inference telemetry (prefix/KV cache logs, invocation metadata) and a high-level KMS custody/residency matrix for keys used in your runtime (who holds keys, where they are backed up, and whether any subprocessor has access).

To keep our audit on schedule, could you provide: 
- CSV listing of runtime subprocessors with service role, region residency, and whether they have telemetry access
- PDF matrix showing KMS custody (Redwood KMS, partner KMS, HSMs, on-prem escrow) and any delegated access controls

We accept redacted exports for IPs/hosts where necessary, but we need explicit answers for: whether any third party can read raw telemetry, whether ephemeral keys are shared, and whether any telemetry is stored outside your VPCs.

Target timeline: can you deliver by EOD Wed (2027-07-21)? If you need a separate NDA/PSA amendment, flag us.

Thanks,
Helen Park
Senior Security Manager — NovaMed
helen.park@novamed.com

Hi Helen — thanks for the clear ask.

Quick note on scope: when you say "telemetry" are you focused on token-level traces/prefixes and invocation metadata, or also aggregated runtime metrics (latency, GPU utilization)? We can produce both, but the subprocessor access question is most relevant for token/prefix-level traces.

Plan: Ben will pull the runtime subprocessor roster and export a CSV with the fields you requested. Karthik will prepare the KMS custody/residency matrix and we will include a short narrative on ephemeral key handling for runtimes.

We should be able to get the CSV + matrix to you by Tue EOD (2027-07-20). If that works I will send an interim packet with the CSV and a link to the KMS matrix.

One ask: please confirm if a redacted CSV is acceptable (we will mask internal hostnames and IPs).

Regards,

Hello Helen — attaching the exports we discussed. See the two files attached to this message: 
- redwood_runtime_subprocessors.csv (columns: subprocessor_name, service_role, region_residency, telemetry_access_level, contract_version, onboarding_date)
- kms_residency_matrix_v1.pdf (visual matrix + short notes on key custody and HSM partners)

Summary highlights (short):
- No subprocessors have access to raw token-level prefixes by default. Runtime telemetry that contains live prefixes is processed only in-memory on customer-dedicated pods; persistent exports are disabled unless customer enables a diagnostic export.
- Ephemeral keys: runtime sessions use short-lived session keys generated from our KMS. Those session keys are never exported to subprocessors.
- Persistent key custody: Redwood controls the root KMS in our primary regions. We use a partner-managed HSM for backup escrow in EMEA; the partner has no runtime-read access to telemetry.

If you need schema notes for the CSV or a mapping doc, I can add a short README.

Best,
Ben Carter
Security Engineering — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

If you can drop those two items into the same Drive link and ping us, we will mark this item as satisfied in our SIG3 intake. We do not need further redaction.

Also, thanks for the fast turnaround — Tuesday timeline was great.

Cheers,
Helen
